title: Null with String and Object overloads
answer: `getData(String)` is selected. The null literal is applicable to both reference-type overloads, but `String` is more specific than `Object`, so Java chooses the String overload. This differs from overloads on unrelated reference types, where passing null may be ambiguous. The decision is made at compile time based on overload specificity; it is not a runtime null dispatch rule.
